full_judgment: 2. Plaintiff's case, in short, is that, the suit jote comprising of 14.53 acres of land, appertains to CS Khatian 82 within Mouza Mailmara, Batiaghata, Khulna, originally belonged to Obhiram Sarder and Rupchand Sarder in equal share. Plaintiffs-predecessor Arjun Mondal, Fakir Mondal, Sonatan Mondal, Chandra Kanta Mondal and Jogheswar Mondal were bargadars under Obhiram and others and accordingly, their names were recorded as dakhalders in respect of 11.76 acres of land in the relevant record. Rupchand died leaving behind two sons namely. Ram Charan Sarder and Ram Krishna Sarder. Obhiram died leaving behind two sons namely, Gurucharan and Ramkanta Sarder. There was a dispute in between Gurucharan and others with that of plaintiffs' predecessor and to settle the dispute a bandabasta was made in respect of the suit property by a registered kabala dated 17-5-39 with the stipulation that the predecessor of the plaintiffs would deliver them either 60 shali paddy or a sum of Rs 300.00 annually. Plaintiffs as the successive heirs of aforesaid Arjun Mondal and others have possessed the suit land. The defendants on 1-11-86 threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land. Hence the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 78 of 1986 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge 2nd Court, Khulna for declaration of their title to the suit land. In that suit defendants 14 to 16 in their written statement, filed on 27-6-87, disclosed that in pursuance of the aforesaid ex parte rent decree, the suit property was auction sold in execution of the said decree and on the basis of the auction purchase they claimed title to the suit land. Plaintiffs having come to know the aforesaid rent suit and the auction sale for the first time from the aforesaid written statement of the defendants, filed the present suit alleging, inter alia, that one of their predecessors namely, Fakir Mondal, a judgment debtor of the rent suit, had died on 28-12-39 before institution of the said rent suit, hence the rent decree and the alleged auction sale, held thereunder are nullity and that the alleged auction purchaser was never in possession of the suit land.
